notes: Modified cash basis for governmental funds; proprietary funds on the accrual basis (depreciation, receivables); the Statement of Activities business-type column ties to the proprietary statement (net position 2,758,047 -> 2,838,696), so business-type lines come from the proprietary statement (p6) by cost type and business_type uses net position (as FY2023/FY2024). Governmental lines from the 2022 Total Governmental Funds column (p4); fund balance rolls forward exactly (1,671,293 + 1,438,054 - 957,640 + 226,085 - 246,108 = 2,131,684). Cash and investments printed separately on the governmental funds statement of assets (p3, 2022 and 2021 comparative Total columns). 'Sales and miscellaneous taxes' 341,130 = Statement of Activities Sales taxes 341,130 (p2). Capital outlay 48,195 is in the Other Governmental Funds column; Statement of Activities Culture and recreation 253,515 = 205,320 + 48,195, and the Pool (41,445) and Library (6,750) schedules print it, so Culture/Recreation. Capital improvements 239,649 entirely in the Street Fund column -> Capital Outlay: Streets/Highways. Utility 'Other operating revenues' 147,750 is counted in Charges for Services on the Statement of Activities. Business-type receipts total = operating 549,781 + interest 147 (no single printed total); disbursements 489,302 as printed on the Statement of Activities (p2) = operating 488,506 + interest 796. Proprietary cash flow statement (pp7-8) printed but left null as in the later years. Balance sheet: government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1); the governmental funds statement includes due to/from other funds 383,811, so its totals do not equal the government-wide figures. Detail: budgetary comparison schedules for all eleven funds (pp9-19, actual budgetary-basis column); lines with '-' actual omitted (budget-only capital outlay and transfers); Meter Deposit schedule prints no revenue or expenditure totals.
